name: Coaxial plug and socket
summary: A plug and socket pair with concentric inner and outer contacts, used to connect coaxial cables to equipment.
description: The coaxial plug and socket shows a connector that mates both the centre conductor and the outer conductor of a coaxial cable. In power and control systems it appears on GPS antenna inputs for time synchronisation, partial-discharge and RF sensors, and video or radio links.

The symbol does not tell you the connector series, impedance or gender convention, which vary between product families. A 50 ohm connector mated to a 75 ohm cable will work poorly, so the connector type should be stated. Outer conductor earthing through the connector body is often implicit and should be checked.
readingNotes: Read connector series and impedance in the annotation.
Check how the outer conductor is earthed at the equipment.
drawingChecklist: Show outer conductor earthing where it matters.
distinction: A coaxial plug and socket mates concentric contacts; an ordinary plug and socket pair mates single pins.
